scope: R8 response to all 11 research/SoK criticisms and writing/submission details; source verification does not imply security efficacy.

items.issue: Purposive corpus size 25/60 was at risk of being described as recall.
items.action: State that it is lexical query/snapshot recovery over a purposively assembled seed-and-snowball corpus, not field-wide recall.
items.remaining: Do not reuse the 25/60 fraction as recall in abstract or response letter.

items.issue: 39 records and 180 audited cells could be mistaken for independent human blind review.
items.action: Identify author verification and AI-assisted initial drafts; separate historical agreement columns from final adjudication.
items.remaining: No independent human blind recoding or independent kappa is available.

items.issue: Author-constructed cases could be overclaimed as external validation.
items.action: Describe the 24 constructed cases and seven mechanism checks as rule/mechanism checks, not independently sampled validation.
items.remaining: No external sampled cases or independent decision set.

items.issue: R1–R9 may be read as universal paper-quality/security scores, including inapplicable hardware or service families.
items.action: Define R1–R9 as reuse evidence conditions; mark applicability per scoped claim and retain NA separately.
items.remaining: No inference about overall study quality from these dispositions.

items.issue: R4/R5 or R8 unreported cells may be read as failed experiments.
items.action: Distinguish NR-R from NR-V and NA; R8 has 11 NR-R, not 11 failed families. The matrix’s separate 11 question marks are unverified bindings.
items.remaining: Preserve distinct labels in any summary chart.

items.issue: SoK emphasis should be the populated evidence synthesis, not a new defense component or theorem.
items.action: Frame the contribution around result-record binding, cross-record transfer errors, and the evidence map.
items.remaining: No new general defense theorem is claimed.

items.issue: The 58-family map and 20-family mitigation audit should remain distinct and visible.
items.action: Retain the full 58-core map and the scoped 20-family R1–R9 matrix, with six contextual and 32 map-only families explained.
items.remaining: No known coverage gap identified in the current main input closure.

items.issue: Contribution needs three concrete cross-record transfer errors.
items.action: Use upstream B shaping vs new frontend B emission; read-only WRA cover vs stateful AHB actions; and borrowed utility/cost or same A call projection vs state claims.
items.remaining: These are record-level corrections, not new theorems or cross-vendor generalization.

items.issue: Origin A/B may be misunderstood as inferring receiver access or threat polarity.
items.action: Define A/B as signal-generation origin only; explicitly separate receiver projection, polarity, and state effects.
items.remaining: Do not use A/B as a proxy for permission or deployment portability.

items.issue: E9 operation-category localization risks implying unrelated private-attribute inference.
items.action: State label coupling: target labels the intended write operation; inference localizes an operation signature and does not prove writes generally reveal unrelated attributes.
items.remaining: Keep oracle selection explicitly diagnostic and non-deployable.

items.issue: E9/E10 customer support, task repeats, and post-hoc chronology need explicit limits.
items.action: Report customer counts, positive customers, known-cohort access, post-hoc status, and intervals conditional on fitted predictions.
items.remaining: No new-customer confirmation.

items.issue: R8 customer-cluster sensitivity requested with all positive-customer deletions.
items.action: Recompute saved-prediction cluster sensitivity across 12 cells and 192 deletions; no model refits or new data. Main text now reports customer-equal and deletion values; S23 contains the full table and checks.
items.remaining: Fixed-prediction sensitivity omits attacker-refitting uncertainty and does not create new customers.

items.issue: Cluster-deletion values could be presented as a confidence interval or independent population estimate.
items.action: Label ranges as deterministic leave-one-positive-customer influence ranges, not CIs; retain 53 customers/345 episodes denominator. Main text now reports customer-equal and deletion values; S23 contains the full table and checks.
items.remaining: Fixed-prediction sensitivity omits attacker-refitting uncertainty and does not create new customers.

items.issue: Same-operation sensitive-attribute analysis risks false positive or overgeneralized attribute inference.
items.action: Keep the exploratory diagnostic limited to 15 customers/20 instances and report observed raw suite maximum 30.3% and shuffled-label maximum 65.2% without claiming positive attribute leakage. E16 is now integrated into the main text and S23 with all negative controls and exact score validation.
items.remaining: Only 15 customers/20 instances; no stable non-action-attribute result or new-population confirmation.

items.issue: Sensitive-attribute labels may reflect action-template or customer confounding.
items.action: Retain availability/confounding analyses and shuffled-label control; state that the control can itself produce high finite-sample maxima.
items.remaining: No causal or semantic-attribute inference claim.

items.issue: R8 E14 comparisons should expose a common seven-attacker suite.
items.action: Report common seven results alongside the full strongest union; reselect the suite maximum in bootstrap draws.
items.remaining: Common-seven sensitivity is not an arbitrary-attacker security proof.

items.issue: WT point comparisons must report cost and avoid global dominance or equal-utility claims.
items.action: Report byte/call ratios and BA points; describe selected point-metric comparisons and explicitly disclaim statistical dominance/equal utility.
items.remaining: WT is an offline RPC adaptation; no live-planner utility measurement.

items.issue: Flush detector performance could be mistaken for intent recovery.
items.action: Separate record-level flush-phase detection from task-category attack and cover-vs-real request classification.
items.remaining: Do not equate 90.4/92.3% flush BA with intent inference.

items.issue: Suffix stripping attack should be reported as performed, with honest limits.
items.action: Describe training-fitted boundary estimation, prefix stripping, composed intent attack, strongest return point, and union retaining stripped/unstripped traces.
items.remaining: No ground-truth oracle filtering presented as deployable.

items.issue: Utility standard should apply consistently to the literature and this paper’s own defenses.
items.action: Separate native undefended reward, replay response/state conformance, and live defended-planner utility.
items.remaining: No live defended LLM re-planning utility measured.

items.issue: E13 RPC latency must not be represented as live defended LLM utility or end-to-end latency.
items.action: Limit clocks to local RPC chain and exclude LLM generation, WAN, deadlines, and replanning.
items.remaining: A new live defended-planner study would be needed for that claim.

items.issue: Luna alias replication could be overcalled as independent confirmation or a new setting.
items.action: Describe it as a same-provider alias and same retail environment; retain smaller suite/training limitations.
items.remaining: No new customer population, provider, environment, or independent confirmation.

items.issue: Luna workflow fit and tool attempts need accurate denominators.
items.action: Retain all 150 runs, 75 per prompt, failures/errors; distinguish dispatch attempts from successful actions and disclose 29 training rows/GB constant behavior.
items.remaining: No claim that 150 runs means 150 per prompt or independent customers.

items.issue: Citation status needs to describe bibliography form without inventing publication status.
items.action: Inventory 77 current citation forms; classify 49 arXiv-only, 21 venue-labelled including 5 with preprint, 1 book, 2 standards, 4 vendor docs; zero unknown after fixing Jiao generator rule.
items.remaining: Labels are not independent peer-review certification; bounded official checks do not prove unlisted preprint papers are unpublished.

items.issue: Early Bird venue versus arXiv citation form must be distinguished.
items.action: Retain venue-labelled-with-preprint for current TIFS citation with consulted arXiv version.
items.remaining: No claim that an arXiv version was the only publication form.

items.issue: Anonymous source bundle should contain only manuscript and supplement sources.
items.action: Created and independently scanned 101-member anonymous paper/source ZIP, including current main and supplement PDFs, source closure and IEEE class/style; excluded Git history and machine logs.
items.remaining: This is not the complete experimental artifact or anonymous hosting; author final review is still needed.

items.issue: Full data anonymized hosting cannot be claimed from a source-only bundle.
items.action: Separate anonymous paper-source packaging from complete data/artifact hosting.
items.remaining: Authors must choose and configure an anonymous repository/host for the complete shareable artifact and verify access.

items.issue: AI assistance disclosure should match what was actually used.
items.action: Keep AI assistance and author verification distinct; do not imply independent human coding.
items.remaining: Disclosure must be checked against venue instructions at submission.

items.issue: AI registration/disclosure draft requested for submission workflow.
items.action: Drafted an explicit AI-use submission statement and its factual author-review prerequisites in the R8 submission document; no HotCRP statement submitted.
items.remaining: Final author inspection, registration and attestation are author actions, not completed by PDF validation.

items.issue: Main-text narrative, tables, counts, and terminology should be internally consistent.
items.action: Review actual main input closure for A/B semantics, R1–R9 applicability, the separate 11 NR-R and 11 unverified matrix cells, and current citation counts.
items.remaining: Final rendered-page and release checks are separately bound to the delivered PDF hashes.

items.issue: No generic claim that leakage reduction, attack chance-level points, or state equality proves defense effectiveness.
items.action: Retain evaluated-suite threshold caveat, fitted-suite scope, and explicit absence of security guarantee/live utility proof.
items.remaining: Do not weaken these limits in the abstract or conclusion.

items.issue: Pre-registration, independent validation, and confirmation language must reflect chronology and provenance.
items.action: Use author-recorded mechanism checks, frozen E9 calibration, and post-hoc E10–E14 labels; do not call existing known-cohort analysis independent or externally blind.
items.remaining: No preregistered external human study or new-customer confirmation.

items.issue: Observer placement and the trusted gateway boundary need an explicit deployment argument.
items.action: Added operator/VPC/relay access assumptions and excluded the marker-aware executor/commit logs; these are visibility assumptions, not prevalence measurements.
items.remaining: No measured deployment prevalence or production deployment.

items.issue: Provider sandboxes, dry-run and rollback were only proposed, not measured.
items.action: Labeled the provider-specific options as feasibility examples; only the local gateway was measured.
items.remaining: Real provider-backend integration and execution measurement remain absent.

items.issue: Database equality and planner-visible equivalence are constructed invariants.
items.action: Reclassified state/response results as implementation-conformance checks, separated from independent empirical utility.
items.remaining: No live defended-planner utility claim.

items.issue: Per-call padding must not be conflated with full traffic-flow confidentiality.
items.action: Distinguished per-call frames from complete fixed-horizon transport cover; dummy tunnel cells execute no tools, and passive-link protection does not require application-layer shadow calls.
items.remaining: No tuned minimum-cost tunnel or blanket shadow advantage.

items.issue: The author-chosen absolute gate is unconfirmed, and paired reduction is not security.
items.action: Retained the frozen gate, labeled it an engineering screen and made unsupported security certification explicit. SoK claims use record-specific transfer failures.
items.remaining: A new, adequately powered customer cohort and defensible deployment-risk target would be needed for a security-efficacy claim.

items.issue: WF adaptations are not full reproductions of original algorithms and guarantees.
items.action: Main text states missing symmetric WT pairing, training-IAT WTF-PAD, simulated-versus-measured clocks and common-suite versus larger-union differences.
items.remaining: Full original-protocol WF reproduction and equal live planner utility are not established.

items.issue: Saved-prediction intervals omit attacker training uncertainty.
items.action: Explained this in main/supplement and preserved all fitted-conditional intervals; added only explicitly deterministic influence analyses.
items.remaining: Nested refitting uncertainty and independent population replication remain unmeasured.

items.issue: Distinct BA effects and byte multipliers appear contradictory without cohorts.
items.action: Added the E9/E10/E13 denominator table, fixed TLS1.2 2.18 versus TLS1.3 2.19 explanation, and retained historical numbers only in their original scope.
items.remaining: No pooling of incompatible observation/attacker/serialization estimands.
